progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: From v02: the structure and function of the cell wall, chloroplast, vacuole, mitochondria, lysosomes and the other named organelles. From v01: eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Stage 5 (assumed, restated in a sentence where used): plants make their own food using light, animals eat food; photosynthesis makes glucose and respiration releases energy from it (word level). Not assumed: autotroph, heterotroph, cellulose, cell sap, turgor pressure.
progression.startsWith: Last time, we opened up a eukaryotic cell and gave every organelle a job. Here are two of them side by side: a cell from a leaf, and a cell from an animal. Most of the parts match. But the leaf cell is boxy and green, and the animal cell is round and soft. Is that just a quirk, or could you predict it from what each cell has to do?
progression.stopsAfter: naming the shared eukaryotic structures (membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, ER, Golgi body); contrasting plant and animal cells through three plant-only structures, each tied to the plant's way of life (autotroph, fixed in place, no skeleton): chloroplasts capture light to make glucose (found in photosynthetic cells, such as leaf mesophyll, not in the underground root cell shown), the rigid cellulose wall and the large central vacuole together give turgor pressure, so cells are firm rather than burst and the plant stays upright; explaining an animal cell's lack of a wall (flexible, can change shape and engulf), its small temporary vacuoles and its lysosomes; explaining that plant cells also have mitochondria because they respire the glucose they make, day and night; writing each difference for both cells with its reason.
progression.nextLesson: a bacterium, with no nucleus and no organelles (route entry bio-y11-fa1-v04).

teaching.task: *Could you predict a plant cell's extra structures from what the plant cell needs to do?*
teaching.causalExplanation: Here's a clue. Forget to water a pot plant, and it droops. Water it, and often within a few hours it stands up again. A plant has no bones and no muscles, so what's holding it up? The answer is sitting inside its cells. Start with what they share. Plant and animal cells are both eukaryotic, so both have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus. Both have mitochondria, ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum and a Golgi body. That's the shared toolkit. The differences are a short list: the leaf cell adds a cell wall, chloroplasts and one large central vacuole. So why exactly those three? Look at how each organism lives. A plant is an autotroph, which means it makes its own food, using light energy. It's also fixed in one spot, and it has no skeleton to hold it up. An animal is a heterotroph: it gets its food by eating other living things. It moves around, and many animals are held up by a skeleton. Every difference we're about to see follows from those two ways of life.

teaching.understandingCheck: So here's a prediction for you. This cell comes from a root, deep underground. It's still a plant cell. Does it have chloroplasts? Have a think. Two exam questions. First. A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria, a cellulose cell wall and a large central vacuole, but no chloroplasts. Identify the type of cell, and justify your answer. Then explain why this cell may have no chloroplasts, yet still needs mitochondria. Pause here to answer. Second. A student says, plant and animal cells differ only because plants are green. Assess this statement, by contrasting the two cell types based on the function of each cell. Pause here to answer.

scenes.visualReference: docs/production/claude-pm/lessons/bio-y11-fa1-v03.md#scene-9: the board returns; the Cam pushes into the animal cell. On "flexible cell membrane" a coded line traces the membrane, label "membrane: the outer boundary", and gently ripples. On "Watch this white blood cell" the phagocytosis set from bio-m7-b06 fills the centre: m7-macrophage-engulf-before-v1.png (grey tag "white blood cell (macrophage); bacterium drawn larger than real"), cross-fading on "wraps it up" to m7-macrophage-engulf-wrap-v1.png and on "pulls it inside" to m7-macrophage-engulf-after-v2.png. Transitions follow bio-m7-b06 Revision 3: each change is a short cross-fade (about 6 frames) or masked over the bacterium, and the change into the after plate is always masked, so the rod never appears twice. On "A cell with a rigid wall couldn't do that" a small plant cell thumbnail appears beside it with its wall ringed and a grey chip "rigid wall: fixed shape". On "small, temporary vacuoles" the animal cell's small vesicles are ringed. On "lysosomes" the set cross-fades to m7-macrophage-engulf-digest-v1.png and the merging lysosomes are ringed, gloss "lysosome: sac of digestive enzymes". Small grey screen tag under the animal header: "many animal cells: centrioles (help organise cell division; later video)". The ledger's "cell wall" row gains under the animal column: "no: flexible, can engulf". At most three bright items. Hold one second.

scenes.visualReference: docs/production/claude-pm/lessons/bio-y11-fa1-v03.md#scene-10: the board returns. On "trap" a WrongChip writes "plant cells have no mitochondria". On "Yes, they do" the chip takes a scribble cross and both plates' mitochondria are ringed in amber, with b6a-mitochondrion-v1.png opening in a callout from the plant cell. On "Making glucose stores energy" a coded arrow runs from a chloroplast to a small grey glucose chip; on "respires the glucose in its mitochondria" the glucose chip breaks down in the cytoplasm and an energy arrow from that breakdown continues into the mitochondrion, out to a chip "energy the cell can use". On "day and night" a small coded sun and moon dial sits above the plant cell: in the sun half both arrows run; as the dial turns to the moon half, the chloroplast arrow stops and the mitochondrion arrow keeps running. On the memory line two handwritten labels write: "kitchen (chloroplast): closes at night" and "furnace (mitochondrion): runs day and night", each with a leader line to its organelle. At most three bright items. Hold one second.
